what_its_for: Mitapivat is used to treat hemolytic anemia in adults with pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency. This is a rare inherited condition where your red blood cells break down too quickly, causing anemia (low red blood cell counts). Mitapivat helps your red blood cells work better and last longer.
how_to_take: Take mitapivat by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, cut, or chew it. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart). Your doctor may increase your dose over time — first to 20 mg twice a day, and then possibly up to 50 mg twice a day — depending on how well it works for you and how you tolerate it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within 6 hours of your scheduled dose time. If more than 6 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mitapivat tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking mitapivat with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers — medicines that can make mitapivat less effective. These include rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, and St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement). Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements. Do not stop taking mitapivat suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause your red blood cells to break down more quickly.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden worsening of anemia or extreme tiredness, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, rapid heartbeat or shortness of breath, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, or any unusual or bothersome side effects. If you need to stop mitapivat, your doctor will slowly lower your dose — do not stop on your own.
when_it_works: Some patients may start to see improvements in their red blood cell counts (hemoglobin levels) within the first few weeks of treatment. However, the full benefit may take several weeks to months. Your doctor will check your blood regularly to see how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Mitapivat may harm an unborn baby. If you can become pregnant, use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one week after your last dose. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. It is not known if mitapivat passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. Fertility: Mitapivat may affect fertility in males and females — talk to your doctor if this is a concern. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Children: Mitapivat is currently approved only for adults. Always tell all of your healthcare providers that you are taking this medicine.
